text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali says Jordan supports a four-way Middle East summit and wants the suffering of Iraqi people to be lifted.
- Nine small centrist political parties elect temporary leadership after merging.
- Deputy Prime Minister Abdullah Ensour tells ministries not to accept any documents or qualifications presented by employees after they have already been appointed.
- Israeli Labour Party member Yossi Beilin in Jordan today for talks with Majali, Crown Prince Hassan, and Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawneh.
- King Hussein returns to Jordan after visit to Oman.
- Finance and supply ministry sources uncover corruption in purchases of subsidised cattle fodder.
- King Hussein and Sultan Qaboos of Oman confirm the need to implement peace.
- Hamas political leader Musa Abu Marzook arrives in Jordan from United States with the king's permission.
- Authorities will prosecute between 20 to 25 companies whose financial irregularities run into hundreds of millions of dinars.
- Majali, in Qatar, calls on U.S. to 'stop its support' for Israel. Jordan, Qatar sign cooperation agreement.
- Fist fights break out in Shmeisani, wealthy area of Amman. Machinegun fired in the air.
- New Israeli ambassador arrives in Amman.
- Baqoura Park to be inaugurated today. Jordan to send a low-level delegation to the site where a Jordanian soldier shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls in March.
- Jordan steps up efforts to attract foreign investment.
